Nov 2
The famed Pushkar camel fair starts on the fourth so I walked into the desert to see the rumpas. There were ~~[illegible]~~ thousands of camels just hanging out shitting. Its pretty fucking cool. They also have some lame rides and ferris wheels but the really cool part is the camels everywhere you look.

I've been a lot more mellow since the acid. It wasn't the trip. It didn't even kick in that heavy. It was just from the whole feeling I got when I put the tab in my mouth. I've now got a more relaxed, go with the flow attitude about things. I live more day to day and worry about stuff less. It's a nice feeling. I've sort of decided to let whatever happens, happen. It's not even so much of a decision, because as much as I'd like to be able to make decisions like that, I can't. It's more just a way I'm moving to. The only thing I've really decided is that I'd like more acid.

We went on camels through' the desert from about 4-6pm. The desert is sandy and flat but there's a lot of shrubbery for what you picture a desert to be. The camels hurt your ass but it was an ok ride. We broke camp on an area where there was about 500 yds of real sand dunes. The site was awsome. I don't usually use words like magical, but that's about the only description I can give.

This was the only day where you wake up and go to sleep in the desert so it was really like being on a camel safari. I got more into the camel thing especially when I took a bhang cookie after lunch.
